newsitem.title: USA: Holiday retail sales seen lower than expected.
newsitem.headline: Holiday retail sales seen lower than expected.

text.p: Retail sales during the holiday season were better than last year, but business at most stores probably fell short of expectations, analysts said Monday.

"This year's sales were at the lower end of expectations for (retail) corporations," said Saul Yaari, an analyst at Piper Jaffray Inc. "Most of them wanted to post high single-digit gains. But we think it was in the 4 to 5 percent range."
In November, analysts' estimates indicated an overall holiday sales gain of between 5 percent and 5.5 percent.
Dain Bosworth analyst Alan Rifkin agreed that sales were mostly good, though upper-end retailers did not fare as well.

"This was a decent Christmas," he said. "Overall sales climbed about 4 percent compared with a year ago. All of the retailers came back from a really poor 1995, except for the real high-end companies like Gucci and Saks."
Several leading retailers, including Wal-Mart Stores Inc., Sears, Roebuck and Co., J.C. Penney Co. Inc. and Dayton Hudson Corp., are expected to report sales for the holiday period within 10 days.
Christopher Vroom, a retail analyst at Alex. Brown & Sons, expects sales gains of between 3.5 percent and 4.5 percent compared with sales a year ago.

"Overall, what we're getting is not a spectacular Christmas selling season but certainly a better one than last year," said Howard Eilenberg, an analyst at Redbook Research, a unit of Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc.
"I spoke to May Department Stores Co. and Federated Department Stores Inc. ... and their business was on plan or better for the last week," Eilenberg said.
May expected same-store sales to climb by 1 percent, while Federated saw December same-store sales ranging between a 1 percent decline and a 1 percent gain.
Eilenberg said May's sales were ahead of expectations for the month to date, while Federated's sales were in line with forecasts. Company officials were unavailable for comment.
Wal-Mart, the nation's largest retailer, said last week that discount and warehouse sales were at the low end of expectations for the holidays just before Christmas.

"Our sales were on plan in the days just before and after Christmas," Shauna Matthews, a Wal-Mart spokeswoman, said. "And we will probably announce a mid-single-digit comparable-sales gain for our discount and warehouse stores." Compaarable sales refer to sales from stores open at least a year.
